chapter_meta_description: After surviving the water horror, Li Huowang wakes to find the crew worshipping him as a dragon king. Explosive rage, a phantom Yang Na, and a bloody self-surgery follow. Apricot Island awaits, but finding Zhuge Yuan will cost him a piece of himself.

og_description: Li Huowang carves bone from his own arm to find Zhuge Yuan.

twitter_description: After the monster, the worshipers. Li Huowang kicks over the altar and pulls out his own bone.

surfaces: True Sutra of the Fire Vestments
lore_anchors.definition: A sacred text of the Ao-Jing Sect that, when burned, releases a fire-slug for agonizing, flesh-sealing healing.
A spectral Zuowandao trickster who now serves as Li Huowang’s captive advisor; her voice is sharp, sarcastic, and constantly weary.
In the Dao-Twisted World, human bone is considered a potent medium for seeking fate or locating a person, particularly using one’s own bone for direct sympathetic connection.
A vast island, said to be half the size of Jiangnan province, where Zhuge Yuan has asked Li Huowang to find him.
A popular folk water deity in Chinese mythology; the boat crew mistakenly worships Li Huowang as one due to his tentacled appearance.
In some dark folk traditions, children are offered in sacrifice to appease river deities; Li Huowang reacts with fury when he sees this.
